public_rationale: The condition held. In its S-1 filed October 26, 2026, Anthropic says it has 'consistently operated in a compute-constrained environment where customer demand exceeds available compute'. On April 14, 2026, Fortune reported that Anthropic had a series of recent outages as usage grew and had introduced stricter peak-hour usage limits. The checkable parts of the claim also hold. A Wayback capture of Anthropic's status page from May 6, 2026, the post date, showed 90-day uptime of 98.73% for claude.ai, which is below two nines. The API (99.05%), Console (99.15%) and Claude Code (99.22%) were just above 99%. On April 6, 2026, Anthropic said the number of business customers each spending over $1 million on an annualized basis had gone from over 500, as stated at its February Series G announcement, to more than 1,000. That shows Anthropic adding large accounts during the period. Main-service availability near or below 99% fits the contract's reading of 'struggles to keep its services at above two nines'. 'Greed' and 'choosing' are moral judgments and are not graded.
limitations: Only the factual parts are graded. 'Unbridled greed' and 'choosing' are opinion.
The uptime figures are Anthropic's own status-page numbers and may count partial degradation differently from third-party monitors.
The customer evidence covers only business customers spending over $1 million on an annualized basis, from February to April 6, 2026. It does not give total customer counts for the whole period.
The capacity evidence comes from a news report and a later company filing. Neither measures capacity directly.

"it's choosing to solve said crunch through sheer, unbridled greed"

our_interpretation: The condition is whether Anthropic faced a real capacity shortage around the time of the post.
'Greed' and 'choosing' are moral judgments and are not graded. The checkable parts are (a) that Anthropic kept adding customers and (b) that it struggled to keep availability above 99% ('two nines').
'Struggles to keep above two nines' is read as measured availability of its main services near or below 99%, not as a requirement that every service fell below 99%.
The period is the roughly 90 days before the post (about February 5 to May 6, 2026), which matches the window Anthropic's status page reports.
criteria.support_condition: Anthropic faced a capacity shortage; its status page showed availability for its main services at or just around 99% in the period; and it reported growing customer numbers in the same period.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Availability for Anthropic's main services was comfortably above 99% (for example 99.9%), or Anthropic was not adding customers in the period.
